title: Freckleton Air Disaster
summary: At approximately 10:36 on 23 August 1944, two newly refurbished B-24 aircraft departed Base Air Depot No. 2 on scheduled test flights. Test pilot First Lieutenant John Bloemendal was flying an aircraft designated Classy Chassis II. The pilots flew north at low altitude and encountered a violent incoming thunderstorm with reduced visibility. Both pilots were ordered to land at once at 10:41 a.m. First Lieutenant Bloemendal, flying at low altitude with reduced visibility, began struggling against violent turbulence and ordered his co-pilot to gain altitude. The aircraft crashed into the centre of the village of Freckleton, Lancashire, killing all three crewmen and 58 individuals on the ground, including 38 children. An official inquiry was unable to pinpoint an exact cause but noted the report was unable to discount structural failure in extreme weather conditions.
probable_cause: An official inquiry was unable to pinpoint an exact cause for the accident, although the report was unable to discount structural failure of the aircraft in such extreme weather conditions as a factor for the accident.

events.text: At approximately 10:36 on the morning of 23 August 1944, two newly refurbished B-24 aircraft departed Base Air Depot No. 2 on scheduled test flights.
Both pilots encountered a violent incoming thunderstorm with reduced visibility immediately south-southeast of the airfield.
The control tower ordered both pilots to land at once on runway 08 at the airfield.
First Lieutenant Bloemendal, flying at a low altitude and with reduced visibility, began struggling against violent turbulence and ordered his co-pilot to gain altitude.
The aircraft crashed into the centre of the village of Freckleton, Lancashire, killing all three crewmen aboard the aircraft and 58 individuals on the ground, including 38 children aged four to six.

notes: Official inquiry unable to determine exact cause
